hints.content:
###Period in sinusoids of the form $y=a\cos(bx+c)+d$

Graphically, the period of a sinusoidal function is the horizontal distance between the ends of a single cycle of its graph.

The period of a sinusoid of the form $y={a}\cos(\maroonD bx + c) + {d}$  is equal to $\dfrac{2\pi}{|\maroonD b|}$. 

 [[☃ explanation 2]]

options.explanation:
Recall that the period of $y=\cos x$ is $2\pi$.  

![A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi over two and the y axis scales by one. The midline is at y equals zero. The highest points on the graph go up to one on the y axis at (zero, one) and (2 pi, one), and the lowest points on the graph go to negative one on the y axis at (pi, negative one). The wave passes through (pi over two, zero) and (three pi over two, zero) on the midline.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/d23bec64829d8698c9e5fe42db114b11b0c6699d)

If $b>0$, the graph of $y=\cos bx$ is a horizontal stretch or compression of the graph of $y=\cos x$.  In particular, if $(v,w)$ is a point on the graph of $y=\cos x$, then $\left(\dfrac{v}{b},w\right)$ is a point on the graph of $y=\cos bx$.  Notice that each $x$-coordinate is divided by $b$, and so the period of the function will also be divided by $b$, or $\dfrac{2\pi}{b}$.  

If $b<0$, the graph of $y=\cos bx$ is a horizontal stretch or compression of the graph of $y=\cos x$ *and* a reflection across the $y$-axis.  A reflection of a sinusoid across the $y$-axis does not affect the period, therefore the period of $y=\cos bx$ is $\dfrac{2\pi}{|b|}$.  

In general, $y=a\cos(bx+c)+d$ is a transformation of the graph of $y=\cos x$.  However, the only transformation that will affect the horizontal distance between the maximum and minimum values (and thus the period) is a horizontal stretch, which is determined by the variable $b$.  

So, the period of $y=a\cos(bx+c)+d$ is the same as the period of $y=\cos bx$, which is equal to $\dfrac{2\pi}{|b|}$.

hints.content:
###Finding the period

The period of  $g(x) = 2\cos(\maroonD{7}x+5)+1$ is:

$\begin{align} \text{period}&=\dfrac{2\pi}{|\maroonD{b}|}\\\\
&=\dfrac{2\pi}{|\maroonD 7|} \\\\\\\\\\
 &= \dfrac{2\pi}{7} \\
 \end{align}$

###The answer

The period of $g(x) = 2\cos({7}x+5)+1$ is $\dfrac{2\pi}{7}$ units.
